errors.description: The taper MAGNITUDE is unverified and appears exaggerated. The drawing, measured on the supplier's own red overlay (which is the welt itself, so no thresholding is involved), gives a taper ratio of 1.15 with depth/run running 0.274 to 0.314 - a gentle convergence. The render's ratio could not be measured: the local-contrast detector returned 290 of 290 columns usable, a suspiciously perfect rate whose cause is that the lapel edge runs diagonally through the measurement box and gets paired with the welt edge. By eye the render's convergence looks more pronounced than 1.15.
errors.expected: A restrained taper of about 1.15 - the welt roughly a seventh deeper at the outboard end than at the inboard one, reading as a gentle convergence rather than a wedge.
errors.actual: Direction correct, magnitude unmeasured and visually stronger than the drawn 1.15.
errors.correction: Measure the render's taper against a box that excludes the lapel edge entirely - start the box outboard of where the lapel edge crosses, and verify the detector is finding the welt's own two edges before trusting any ratio. If the taper is confirmed above roughly 1.3, soften it toward the drawn 1.15 while keeping the deep end at the armhole side.

notes:
Attempt 2. Graded on DIRECTION only; magnitude is explicitly not certified and is the reason this does not pass.

Method note, recorded because it cost four attempts on this single option: the drawing was eventually measured on the supplier's red overlay, which IS the welt, removing all thresholding guesswork. Three earlier measurements were discarded - (1) a raw threshold on the render returned 139px of depth inside a 140px crop box, saturated because navy-on-navy has almost no absolute contrast; (2) a raw threshold on the drawing gave taper 2.31 deeper-at-left and (3) local contrast on the same drawing gave 1.18 deeper-at-right. The disagreement in DIRECTION is what forced the question rather than a choice between them, and the answer was that both were reading lapel edges at x 560-860 when the welt is at x 693-921. Cropping and looking settled it in one glance.

The render measurement remains contaminated by the same class of error, which is why magnitude is reported as unmeasured rather than estimated.
